I didnt play all that long. I just couldn't get passed the card mechanism. I had high hope, since Left 4 Dead.

Back 4 blood is weird. It's not terrible like everyone said but it's not exactly good or even replayable like left 4 dead 2 is all these years later. The only thing back 4 blood has over L4D2 is better graphics and aiming down sights. But the skill system and card crap really is terrible and RNG based so you're almost forced to play a certain way rather than how you want to play.

where killing floor 2 feels intentional, Back 4 blood feels forced. That's the best way i can describe the skill systems and game as a whole. Forced, rushed, and thrown in with no rhyme or reason. It wants to be everything without doing anything or even knowing why it's doing the things it does.

6/10
I’m gonna be honest: if this game wasn’t constantly marketed as the “spiritual successor” to Left 4 Dead, I probably would’ve been much less harsh on it.

But that’s exactly the problem.

You CANNOT spend years telling people that Back 4 Blood is the successor to Left 4 Dead and that it’s made by the creators of Left 4 Dead, then deliver something that completely misses what made those games special in the first place.

Is it a terrible game?
No.

Is it Left 4 Dead 3?
Absolutely not.

The story is okay. The Cleaners are decent enough, the weapons feel good, and there are moments where you can see some genuinely cool ideas buried under everything else.

But man… the vibe just isn’t there.

Left 4 Dead 1 and 2 had this unique atmosphere that made every campaign memorable. The music, the characters, the pacing, the special infected, the simplicity of jumping in with friends and immediately having fun.

Back 4 Blood feels like it looked at Left 4 Dead and said:

“What if we added 37 systems, 12 currencies, card decks, progression trees and a bunch of DLCs?”

Instead of improving the formula, it feels like it overcomplicated it.

And speaking of DLCs…

There are WAY too many paid expansions for a game that never convinced me it deserved them in the first place.

Every time I played, I couldn’t stop comparing it to Left 4 Dead 2, and every single time it made me want to go play Left 4 Dead 2 instead.

That’s probably the biggest criticism I can give.

Not because Back 4 Blood is awful.

But because after a few hours I realized I’d rather replay a 2009 game than continue playing the supposed successor released more than a decade later.

Overall:

Good guns.
Decent story.
Some fun moments.

But as a “spiritual successor” to Left 4 Dead?

Massive disappointment.

It’s not a bad game.

It’s just painfully average living in the shadow of two masterpieces.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that progression requires using a card system to build decks that grant character and weapon bonuses.

citations.review_text:
This game is a good example of how a game can have everything it needs to succeed and still end up being bad because of the devs decisions.

In first few hours the cons start becoming obvious, first thing is the difficulty which feels unbalanced and makes no sense. zombies will sometimes feels like they just pop up out of nowhere like they're some kind of surprise box giving you barely any chance to react or dodge their attacks.

Then there's the unnecessary and complicated card system, you're just gonna end up looking up the best meta on google for best cards deck, and then u gonna forget about it and ull never look at it again.

Weapon upgrade system is also missing, which takes away one of the most important parts of feeling like you're actually progressing. also u'll end up spending more than half the game using the baseball bat or the axe cus you're constantly running out of ammo.

Those are probably the biggest issues with the game, and honestly they should've been avoided completely, but it feels like the devs somehow avoided the game itself instead.

The only situation where I'd tell you to give this game a shot is if you find it at 90% off, at that price it might be worth trying if u're just looking for somthin to play with your friends.

I'm a huge Left 4 Dead fan, so I decided to give Back 4 Blood a try. It was often described as a spiritual successor, or even as Left 4 Dead 3. Unfortunately, it's nowhere near Left 4 Dead.
The biggest positive is that it's a pretty enjoyable zombie shooter. There's a lot happening on screen, the maps are detailed, and at times you can definitely feel the Left 4 Dead vibe. Sadly, that's where my praise ends.
My biggest issue is the card system. You have to collect and build decks that give your character and weapons various bonuses. I simply don't enjoy mechanics like that, so I ignored them completely. It quickly became clear that the game expects you to use this system, because without a proper deck I constantly felt underpowered. In the end, the final boss stopped me, and I never finished the game. The only thing missing was the option to buy a pink weapon skin... although maybe I just didn't find it xD
Another problem is that it's very difficult to find people to play with nowadays. I ended up playing most of the campaign with bots because finding a co-op group was almost impossible. On top of that, the menus and lobby are overloaded with content, making it feel like I'm preparing for a war instead of simply jumping into a game and shooting zombies.
What disappoints me the most is that there's actually a decent shooter hidden underneath all of this. Instead of focusing on the simple, fast-paced gameplay that made Left 4 Dead so fun, the developers added layer upon layer of systems that only made the experience more frustrating for me.
If a game like this can turn away a longtime Left 4 Dead fan and someone who loves zombie shooters, it's hard for me to imagine how it would win over someone who picked it up out of simple curiosity.

Back 4 Blood is in essence a spiritual successor to Left 4 Dead. Developed by the original studio creators of the L4D franchise, it has the same exact core concept: 4 player co-op navigating through hordes of zombie enemies to reach safe room to safe room.

Key Distinct differences: 

Currency, Card System, Aesthetic Purchases, Weapon upgrades and Attachments, Classes

There's a currency system, which allots you the ability to customize your character aesthetically. There's two forms of these, supply line tokens and skull totem tokens, the latter of which you must play a hidden level within the levels. These are used to purchase cards you can make into a deck for the campaign, or purchase cosmetic enhancements to your characters and weapons. Within the campaign itself, there's a separate currency (copper) which allots you the ability to purchase temporary supplies in the level/act, upgrades to your guns. It also allows you the ability to purchase ability cards, which grant your character in the campaign temporary boosts to certain stats.

Weapons are no longer just that weapon, they're customizable with attachments you can find or purchase within the game. There's also unique weapons that come with their own ability and niche.

Each character also has their own unique abilities and bonuses to stats that they bring to the team.

Initially I gave this game a thumbs down, as once I cleared it fully, I pushed to a higher difficulty and was demoralized completely. That part hasn't changed, but there's a lot of added new DLC's and updates to the game that balance some aspects of it that I played and enjoyed.

What I will say is, the difficulty is unbalanced. The game is either too easy on certain difficulties, or impossible on higher ones.

Will I play it again? Probably. Will I enjoy it again? Probably. The fatigue sets in fairly quick though, so try to play it sparingly and with friends.

claims.claim: The game was abandoned by developers with no further updates, new content, or patches planned.

citations.review_text:
## A Great Co-op Shooter That Was Abandoned Too Soon

Back 4 Blood is a genuinely fun co-op shooter with satisfying gunplay, plenty of weapons, and a card system that allows you to create different builds for each character. It is especially enjoyable with a full group that communicates and works together.

✅ **Pros**

• Smooth and satisfying combat
• Fun with a coordinated group
• Plenty of weapons and build options
• Good replay value across different difficulties
• The card system adds variety between runs

❌ **Cons**

• Random teammates can make matches frustrating
• Some difficulty spikes feel unbalanced
• The game was abandoned before reaching its full potential
• No more meaningful updates or new content

The biggest disappointment is not the gameplay itself, but how quickly the developers moved on from it. Back 4 Blood had a strong foundation and could have become much better with continued updates, balancing, and additional content.

Overall, it is still a great game when played with friends, but it is difficult not to think about what it could have become. I recommend picking it up on sale, especially if you already have a group to play with.

It's a decent game but it can only be played once

I really like the card deck mechanic and the wound mechanic which makes you want to avoid taking damage and this game has a lot of potential for fun builds but the problem is the devs abandoned it. There will be no new updates, no new cards, no new maps, nothing.

You will be able to unlock most if not all unique cards throghout the campaign playthrough, or shortly after finishing all missions once, and it just leaves wishing for more. The replayability is not there, yeah, one can say "erm, but you can build new decks with new weapons and new roles?" but that still leaves you with the same levels, same enemies, same everything. I mean, it's just a grind with no goal in sight, unless you're an overachiever enjoying completing hardest difficulties just for your own amusement, it's just not it.

If Steam didn't have a binary review system, I'd give it a 7/10. Yeah, it's alright if you like L4D2 game genre and you have some friends you can pick the game up with when it's at -90% discount but there is no reason to get back to it later after finishing it once which is a bummer, I think devs stopped supporting it too early and it could've been much much better

citations.review_text:
Horrible marketing about being made by "the minds behind Left 4 Dead.", the game isn't that similar aside from the very obvious and mostly downgraded variants of zombies and map design. 

Graphically it's just the generic realism every game strives for; it's boring. Considering the zombie apocalypse, you'd expect everywhere to be much dirtier; it's too clean. Anywhere that had an abundance of filth and debris felt very unnatural and orchestrated.

Gameplay-wise, they had some good ideas, like decks and mutation variants. Mutations aside, they really fumbled the decks' implementation; it could've been a lot more fun but currently just subtracts from the whole experience. Mutations weren't done very well either.

Gunplay is quite floaty and old-feeling; it reminds me of games from the early 2010s. 

Sound is very weak; all weapons, explosions and Ridden (Infected) all sound rather mild and not how they should.

Characters, yeah, they suck. Considering most zombie games have a memorable cast of characters like Chuck Greene, Frank West, Joel, Deacon St. John, Leon Kennedy, Claire Redfield, Clementine and literally anyone in Left 4 Dead, the characters in this game basically have no presence whatsoever.

While everything I've said is true and I stand by it, I've enjoyed playing the game. Just wish they added modding support before leaving it for dead.

This game makes me depressed. It's really fun. Like, really really fun. Sadly it has many flaws, and lacks mod support which would elevate it to insane heights. It's on life support now and nothing will change that. I recommend playing it, but only if you don't mind being sad by the current state of this game's life too.

claims.claim: Difficulty settings feel poorly balanced, with medium being too easy while higher difficulties present sudden, extreme spikes that are near impossible for small groups.

citations.review_text:
Disclaimer for those not in the know: this game isn't L4D2 or a spiritual successor, it's its own thing and should be judged by its own merits, if you were looking for L4D2: imnmediately move away from this game, the following critique is about B4B as a standalone game, unrelated to L4D2.

Despite all of the negativity towards this game, I still gave it a fair shot, and honestly it sucks. At least the game doesn't need you to play 80+ hours to get all the cards anymore, but outside of that QoL it honestly sucks. Here is a basic rundown of every issue I've had in this game, almost all of these issues are exclusive to NM/NH as the difficulties above Veteran are horribly balanced:
- The game is way too luck based, certain combinations of mutations are just "♥♥♥♥ you, lose now" even with the most optimal builds and some combinations just outright end your run if you don't have the right builds
- The AI, while better than launch, still sucks. They get distracted easy and you have to learn how to abuse the AI in obtuse ways (even more obtuse in not full squads). They are also genuinely useless for missions that require carrying items as they can't carry them
- A ton of missions have infinite hordes so bad that they're near impossible to win without a certain amount of firecrackers/pipe bombs
- A ton of cards were nerfed and never buffed so a ton of them just suck now and they abandoned the game so there's no hope of them ever buffing what they nerfed

Other than those gameplay issues, the game is a pretty decent Horde Shooter, it was enjoyable on Veteran (but too easy) but anything above is borderline masochistic as you'd more often than not simply die from random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ than anything of your own fault. NM/NH is the epitome of RANDOM ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GO until the player dies, it isn't satisfying, it isn't fun, it becomes gambling for the one perfect run where everything aligns instead of getting cucked at a random point to random bs you can't counter.

The game also lacks basic…

this game could be so amazing but medium difficulty is waaay too easy, hard is a good challenge but some random levels are suddenly waaay too hard for only 2 players. Both bots die instantly and my girlfriend shoots me in the back all the time :( Apart from that very poorly balanced difficulty which sucks because you can't change the settings during a playthrough.

in our case, we had to play most of the game on a difficulty that made the game insanely easy, just because we couldnt get past one poorly designed 2 minute level.

This game is one of my favorites despite the bad reputation. I am looking forward to a B4B2.

There is little variety in levels as you play the same zones but different routes. However, the Acts are so long, this doesn't bother me too much. 

The Mutants are oddly balanced. They are either a pain or too weak. There are roughly 4 types with 3 variations. It is hard to keep track as the variations have minor visual differences yet the tactics to take them down are slightly different. Reekers are dumb and fun to kill. The Tallboy is wildly overpowered compared to the others because it hides its weakspot. The Spitters are a joke and die easy. The Wailers are either canon fodder or will pin you down.

At first I hated the card system because it made the game feel bloated and overwhelming. Once you get used to it, it's actually really fun the kind of builds you can make. Have a problem with friendly fire? Use "Down in Front" problem solved. 

No cash shop and everything is unlockable (besides DLC) in-game. A lost form in modern games that many will overlook.

The bots are crazy overpowered and with Offline mode, this game can be played solo. Best played with one or two other friends. Once you start playing 4-player, you will notice how good the bots are.

- The AI, while better than launch, still sucks. They get distracted easy and you have to learn how to abuse the AI in obtuse ways (even more obtuse in not full squads). They are also genuinely useless for missions that require carrying items as they can't carry them
- A ton of missions have infinite hordes so bad that they're near impossible to win without a certain amount of firecrackers/pipe bombs
- A ton of cards were nerfed and never buffed so a ton of them just suck now and they abandoned the game so there's no hope of them ever buffing what they nerfed

Other than those gameplay issues, the game is a pretty decent Horde Shooter, it was enjoyable on Veteran (but too easy) but anything above is borderline masochistic as you'd more often than not simply die from random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ than anything of your own fault. NM/NH is the epitome of RANDOM ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GO until the player dies, it isn't satisfying, it isn't fun, it becomes gambling for the one perfect run where everything aligns instead of getting cucked at a random point to random bs you can't counter.

The game also lacks basic…

this game could be so amazing but medium difficulty is waaay too easy, hard is a good challenge but some random levels are suddenly waaay too hard for only 2 players. Both bots die instantly and my girlfriend shoots me in the back all the time :( Apart from that very poorly balanced difficulty which sucks because you can't change the settings during a playthrough.

in our case, we had to play most of the game on a difficulty that made the game insanely easy, just because we couldnt get past one poorly designed 2 minute level.

claims.claim: The card system feels bloated, overwhelming, and confusing when first encountering it.

citations.review_text:
This game is one of my favorites despite the bad reputation. I am looking forward to a B4B2.

There is little variety in levels as you play the same zones but different routes. However, the Acts are so long, this doesn't bother me too much. 

The Mutants are oddly balanced. They are either a pain or too weak. There are roughly 4 types with 3 variations. It is hard to keep track as the variations have minor visual differences yet the tactics to take them down are slightly different. Reekers are dumb and fun to kill. The Tallboy is wildly overpowered compared to the others because it hides its weakspot. The Spitters are a joke and die easy. The Wailers are either canon fodder or will pin you down.

At first I hated the card system because it made the game feel bloated and overwhelming. Once you get used to it, it's actually really fun the kind of builds you can make. Have a problem with friendly fire? Use "Down in Front" problem solved. 

No cash shop and everything is unlockable (besides DLC) in-game. A lost form in modern games that many will overlook.

The bots are crazy overpowered and with Offline mode, this game can be played solo. Best played with one or two other friends. Once you start playing 4-player, you will notice how good the bots are.

Not so good but not so bad, I like it. From my perspective, people didn't like it because they were expecting another Left 4 Dead installment. My only complaint is the card-based perk system that can be confusing and frustrating sometimes, and also, it can feel repetitive.

citations.review_text: Amazing,game  I ve frasturated that developer team gave up on this game

I had very high hopes for this game. I played it during the beta testing and after the full release. The game itself is great, with fun gunplay, especially when you make chaotic decks. That’s the main reason why I like this game — the deck-building mechanic. I had fun playing it with friends and helping them make meme builds.

I would like to rate this game much higher, but sadly it seems they abandoned it.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the player base has declined and multiplayer modes are dead.

citations.review_text:
[h1]Dogsh*t or a gem?[/h1]
[b]Here are 4 reasons not to buy/play Back 4 Blood:[/b]

1. The game won't receive any new updates. The developers posted a "goodbye" statement on Feb 2nd, 2023, in which they wrote that their work on B4B had come to an end and they had moved on to the next project.

2. Multiplayer is almost dead. Even if you can find a few occasional campaign partners, other game modes are completely dead.

3. Questionable design choices:

- No key mapping for the flashlight.
- No server list for multiplayer.
- The multiplayer and singleplayer experiences differ drastically. Playing the game in singleplayer is so much easier that it eliminates the need to play it in multiplayer and team up with other players, even for the hardest difficulty.

4. Performance is not great. The game usually runs smoothly, but sometimes, closer to the end of a level, I was getting ungodly frame drops out of nowhere, which could end my No Hope run in seconds. If you have a high-end PC, however, you have nothing to worry about.


[b]If you're still here :D, here are the reasons why I leave a positive review:[/b]

1. I believe the amount of hate this game received is undeserved. Marketing Back 4 Blood as a Left 4 Dead successor did it no favors, as it attracted thousands of Left 4 Dead supremacist hyenas that started mauling and gnawing B4B for everything that makes it different from Left 4 Dead.

2. I fell in love with the gameplay. It is dynamic, fast-paced, and sometimes unforgiving, but ultimately, extremely fun. If you don't expect it to be Left 4 Dead and just want a fun zombie shooter, you won't be disappointed.

3. I consider the card system to be a nice addition. You don't see this mechanic often in shooters, but in B4B, it is well done and adds an additional layer of complexity.

4. The game looks amazing. Even on medium graphics settings, the game looks pretty. On high-end PCs, the visual aspect is incredible.

The game is good, but never quite managed to get the following that Left 4 Dead had for years. Unfortunately, I'm not sure the playerbase is very populous anymore, but that said, if you can find people, the game is still very enjoyable. The PvP is kind of whatever, but I'm biased towards the L4D formula for PvP.

It is NOT worth the $60 it still wants, though. Not these days anyway. Very worthwhile on a sale, even so.

Great game, although it's quite disappointing the devs gave up on the game seemingly. If they were still active maybe there would be a higher player base. Some bugs and things that need to be tweaked but overall worth the buy.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that players cannot turn the flashlight on manually.

citations.review_text:
The game is decent, but it has some glaring issues. One of the biggest problems is the flashlight. For some reason, you can’t turn it on manually, even though there are areas in the game where you genuinely need it. Not being able to manually control the flashlight is really stupid and frustrating.

I understand that the developers wanted to implement a roguelike mechanic with the card system, but in practice it just feels bad. The RNG can completely ruin runs. One run you’ll breeze through, and the next it feels like the game simply doesn’t want you to progress no matter what you do.

The card shop also feels bad like sometimes when it refreshes, it just gives you the exact same set of cards again and again for no apparent reason. Deck building is also bad because you’re forced to pick cards that work in most situations and cards that are a bit more niche suffer. For example the Acid Resistance card is basically useless most of the time, except for the one moment when the game randomly decides it’s acid time baby. A simple solution would have been to allow 2–3 (maybe even 5) wildcard slots in your deck that you could swap depending on the situation, but apparently that was too much to implement.

Another bad design choice is weak spots. What’s the point of giving enemies weak spots if you’re just going to cover them with armor? Also, we have the the great design of Tallboys where you can’t even see their weak spot from the front lol.

Overall, the game feels like it’s trying too hard to be unique and quirky. A lot of these systems are just useless and frustrating. Also, the jump in difficulty from veteran to nightmare is too big for some reason. Did they forget to balance it or something ? tbh i dont really know but whatever.
